gen-dafont-disorder-gf-savate: Disorder has tails and terminals as thick as its stems, with big lowercase set well apart, while Savate on the other hand shows a faint nib-pressure variation. Sturdy hairlines and open jaws keep a sans body easy going.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-schibsted-grotesk: Raw and chaotic, Disorder holds one constant stroke width throughout. Schibsted Grotesk sits below it with big open e and a shapes and tall bowls, so a longer stretch of text moves along in a friendly, approachable way.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-sen: Disorder lets its oversized lowercase stand well apart, rough and a little wild in every line it draws. And Sen, a plain sans with tall letters and curves that stop before turning inward, gives that noise somewhere tidy to land.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-sintony: Raw wire-cut strokes and big lowercase give Disorder a jagged, chaotic look, with glyphs spaced well apart on the line. Sintony follows with a chunky, smooth sans-serif body.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-sofia-sans: Sofia Sans brings rounded letters with clear open sides and tall lowercase that look like cut acrylic stencil pieces, all in one monoline stroke. Sofia Sans is the quiet, modern anchor here, set against the loud, chaotic Disorder.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-sofia-sans-semi-c: Disorder wears its chaos in oversized lowercase with no swelling where curves meet stems, and every glyph sits well apart. Sofia Sans Semi Condensed gives a clean sans counterpart, its stencil-like line nearly capital height.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-sono: Sono brings tall lowercase, generous letter spacing and a slightly ajar a, which gives a plain sans body room to breathe under the display. Disorder, with its ballpoint-flat line, supplies the raw noise.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-stack-sans-headli: Stack Sans Headline keeps a monoline skeleton and deep middle band, with wide gaps that hold tiny sizes crisp on the page. And Disorder, chaotic and raw with its big lowercase, makes that sans feel even more orderly.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-stack-sans-notch: Stack Sans Notch reads as clean and open, its curves easy to see into and its strokes like rod stock. Disorder then crashes in above it, raw and loose, while the plain sans stays composed.
gen-dafont-disorder-gf-stack-sans-text: Chaotic and raw, Disorder sets big lowercase well apart with no swelling where curves meet stems, while Stack Sans Text carries a marker-like line. Disorder makes noise; Stack Sans Text keeps the sans reading smooth.
